item.title: 2 Teams Emerge As Prefered Destinations for Colton Parayko
item.description: Colton Parayko made his decision earlier today. After the St. Louis Blues agreed on a trade to send him to the Buffalo Sabres late Wednesday, the 6-foot-6 defenseman decided to invoke his no-trade clause and blocked the deal. But that doesn't mean he won't agree to be dealt to a destination of his choosing. Parayko, 32, has spent his entire 11-year NHL career in St. Louis, and he'd prefer to stay. item.title: Maple Leafs Listening to Trade Offers on Matthew Knies
item.description: The Toronto Maple Leafs won't be moving the likes of Auston Matthews and William Nylander, but one shocking name has still surfaced in trade chatter. Sportsnet insider Elliotte Friedman revealed that the team has been quietly listening to offers for winger Matthew Knies as the NHL trade deadline approaches. item.title: Kraken & Panthers Could Become Trade Partners
item.description: The Florida Panthers have entered the fray at the deadline as sellers for the first time in a long time. They executed their first deal on Thursday, trading veteran defenseman Jeff Petry. Then they pulled both Sergei Bobrovsky and AJ Greer from the lineup for Thursday night's game. More trades could be coming. item.title: New York Rangers trade Sam Carrick to Buffalo Sabres
item.description: After being a healthy scratch on Thursday night for the New York Rangers thanks to 'roster management' purposes, fourth-line center Sam Carrick is off to the Buffalo Sabres.Hearing the Rangers will trade Sam Carrick to Buffalo Every team can use some Stouffville— Elliotte Friedman (@FriedgeHNIC) March 6, 2026At the time of filing, the return for Carrick is unknown, however, it's expected to be a mid-round draft pick, or b-level prospect. Carrick, 34, can play either the wing or down the middle.

item.title: Ottawa Senators trade David Perron to Detroit Red Wings
item.description: David Perron is heading back to Motown.The Ottawa Senators and Detroit Red Wings announced a deal on Thursday night that sees Perron head back to the Red Wings in exchange for a 2026 fourth-round pick. Perron, 37, is currently on the injured reserve, and held a 15-team no-trade list as part of his $4 million AAV contract.TRADE ALERT: The #Sens have acquired a conditional 4th round pick in the 2026 NHL Draft from the Detroit Red Wings in exchange for forward David Perron. pic.twitter.com/pwTX0dz7
